description.narrative: Assessment of Project Outcomes - Supplier Effects. The Project is expected to stimulate the local supply chain through the development of novel Amazonian ingredients leveraging biodiversity and by scaling up procurement from the Amazonian bioeconomy. The Amazon rainforest constitutes a vital component of the Earth's natural infrastructure and plays a critical role in regulating the planet's climate system and biodiversity. Despite its ecological significance, Amazon rainforest has witnessed a rise in deforestation rates since 2012, with soybean production and cattle ranching identified as key contributors. Over the past two decades, Natura has cultivated a sustainable value chain within the Amazon biome through collaboration with small-scale agroextractivist communities. The Company sources nearly half of its raw materials from Amazonian suppliers, solidifying its model as a globally recognized example of economic use of the standing forest. Assessment of Contribution to Market Creation - Inclusiveness. At the market level, IFC expects that the Project will incentivize other companies to adopt sustainable sourcing practices from Amazon. This has the potential to unlock economic opportunities for marginalized populations within the region. Collaborating with small-scale agroextractivist communities can improve the livelihoods of these underserved groups, while simultaneously promoting sustainable practices that contribute to the well-being of the Amazon ecosystem.

The investment involves the purchase by IFC, for its own account, of unsecured debt instruments, in a principal amount of BRL300,000,000 with an up to 5 years tenor and bullet principal payment at maturity, issued in the Brazilian capital markets by Natura Cosméticos S.A. (Natura or the Company) (the Project). These debentures will be labelled as sustainability-linked debentures (in accordance with the Sustainability-Linked Bond Principles of 2023, issued by the International Capital Market Association ICMA) with Natura committing to increase its sourcing from the Amazon to 49 new bioingredients by 2027, up from 44 ingredients as of 2023.
